log.text: Floette used Light of Ruin → Tyranitar
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Garchomp

decisions.rationale: Lead the Sand core: Tyranitar sets Sand Stream immediately, and Excadrill at 308 Spe in sand outspeeds the entire opposing roster including Tailwind-boosted Garchomp. Excadrill's Rock Slide is 4x SE on Talonflame (Focus Sash saves it, but sand chip + recoil breaks it) and Iron Head is SE on Mega Floette. Tyranitar's Rock Slide also threatens Talonflame and provides general spread pressure. Gholdengo is the defensive anchor on the bench, resisting Fairy (Floette Moonblast), Dragon (Garchomp), and Water (Milotic Scald) while Make It Rain chips Steel-types like Metagross. Gengar-Mega rounds out the four as a Shadow Tag trapper that resists Fairy, outspeeds most of the field at 178 (165-200 Mega), and can Taunt screen/Tailwind setters or pick off weakened targets with Shadow Ball. This four covers all six opposing mons: sand Excadrill handles Garchomp, Talonflame, Metagross, and Scrafty; Gholdengo walls Floette and Milotic; Gengar-Mega traps and cleans late.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega is Floette-Eternal (Fairy, base 92 Spe, Flower Veil→Mega ability unconfirmed but likely Fairy Aura per build notes). Opponent speed tiers: Talonflame 160-195 (Gale Wings priority Brave Bird), Garchomp 134-169 (Jolly LO), Floette 100-158 (Timid), Milotic 101-133 (Bold), Metagross 90-122 (Adamant), Scrafty 78-110 (Careful). My sand Excadrill at 308 outspeeds all even under opponent Tailwind (max Garchomp ~253). Key SE mappings: Excadrill Rock Slide 4x on Talonflame, Iron Head 2x on Floette, High Horsepower 2x on Metagross. Garchomp Earthquake is spread+ally (hits partner). Milotic Competitive punishes Intimidate—avoid bringing Tauros alongside Milotic. Plan across games: keep Sand core as default lead; adjust backs if opponent adapts (Grimmsnarl if special attackers overwhelm, Tauros if Metagross/Scrafty need Fighting answers). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is wincon for trapping weakened targets.

decisions.rationale: Lead Talonflame + Metagross for reliable Tailwind pressure and immediate Mega Gengar counterplay through Bullet Punch, while preserving Mega Floette until Steel/Poison pressure is weakened. Garchomp remains a strong back-line answer to Tyranitar, Excadrill, and Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 preview plan: Talonflame + Metagross is the default lead for Tailwind plus Bullet Punch pressure into Mega Gengar. Preserve Mega Floette until opposing Steel- and Poison-types are controlled; retain Garchomp as key pressure into Tyranitar, Excadrill, and Gholdengo.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill High Horsepower on Metagross (58.8-104.5%, possible OHKO) plus Tyranitar Rock Slide breaks Talonflame's Focus Sash (guaranteed 4x KO damage → 1 HP) and chips Metagross (9-16%). Sandstorm then KOs Talonflame at 1 HP. Combined Metagross damage (~74-127% with sandstorm) likely KOs it too. This play is robust: if Metagross Protects, I still eliminate Talonflame via Sash break + sandstorm rather than wasting both attacks. If Talonflame Flare Blitzes Excadrill, Sash saves it but sandstorm KOs Excadrill — a favorable 1-for-2 trade. If Talonflame Tailwinds or Brave Birds (NVE), Excadrill survives and I likely sweep both foes. Tyranitar survives Meteor Mash at 9-35% HP and gets Rock Slide off before fainting.

Plan across games: keep Sand core as default lead; adjust backs if opponent adapts (Grimmsnarl if special attackers overwhelm, Tauros if Metagross/Scrafty need Fighting answers). Watch for Metagross Protect and Talonflame Tailwind as opponent adaptations in game 2.

decisions.rationale: Set Tailwind with Gale Wings while protecting Metagross from Excadrill's immediate Ground pressure. Talonflame is highly vulnerable to either Rock Slide, so preserving Metagross and enabling the back line to operate under Tailwind is the safest opening.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan remains to use Tailwind to let Garchomp pressure Tyranitar and Excadrill, while preserving Mega Floette until opposing Steel- and Poison-type pressure is reduced.

decisions.rationale: Bring in Garchomp under Tailwind to immediately pressure both opposing active Pokémon with its Ground STAB while retaining Mega Floette for later once Steel pressure is reduced.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: use Tailwind-supported Garchomp to pressure Tyranitar and Excadrill; preserve Mega Floette until opposing Steel- and Poison-type pressure is reduced.

decisions.rationale: Protect Tyranitar to block Metagross's Meteor Mash (its only meaningful target—all its moves are NVE on Excadrill) while Excadrill hits Metagross with High Horsepower (59-105%, possible KO). If Garchomp Earthquakes, Metagross takes EQ (47-103%) + HHP (59-105%) = near-certain KO, and Excadrill survives via Focus Sash. Metagross Protect is unreliable (used last turn). This preserves the sand setter and removes the Metagross threat in one turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega is Floette-Eternal (Fairy, base 92 Spe, Flower Veil→Mega likely Fairy Aura). Opponent speed tiers: Talonflame 160-195 (Gale Wings priority Brave Bird), Garchomp 134-169 (Jolly LO), Floette 100-158 (Timid), Milotic 101-133 (Bold), Metagross 90-122 (Adamant), Scrafty 78-110 (Careful). My sand Excadrill at 308 outspeeds all non-Tailwind foes; under opponent Tailwind, Garchomp 268-338 can outspeed Excadrill (uncertain). Key damage: Tyranitar Ice Punch 4x on Garchomp (73-131%, possible OHKO), Excadrill HHP 2x on Metagross (59-105%, possible OHKO), Garchomp EQ 2x on Tyranitar (61-87%, not OHKO) and on Metagross (47-103%, possible self-KO—deterrent). Metagross Meteor Mash 2x on Tyranitar (65-91%). All Metagross moves NVE on Excadrill. Milotic Competitive punishes Intimidate—avoid bringing Tauros alongside Milotic. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is wincon for trapping weakened targets. Plan: keep Sand core as default lead; adjust backs if opponent adapts. Watch for Metagross Protect and Tailwind as opponent adaptations in game 2.

decisions.rationale: Bullet Punch chips Tyranitar before Garchomp’s faster Earthquake, maximizing the chance to remove Tyranitar before it can use Ice Punch while Earthquake also forces Excadrill to its Focus Sash.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: leverage Tailwind Garchomp pressure to remove Tyranitar and Excadrill; preserve Floette-Eternal until opposing Steel- and Poison-type pressure is reduced. Opponent Tyranitar has Smooth Rock Sand Stream; Excadrill has Focus Sash Sand Rush.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Go for the potential game-ending double KO: Tyranitar Ice Punch (4x SE, 72.6-131.1% vs Garchomp's 90%) and Excadrill Iron Head (2x SE, 79.6-154.4% vs Floette's 100%). If both connect, opponent has zero Pokémon remaining for an instant Game 1 win. Excadrill at 1% HP is a dead slot regardless — attacking extracts maximum value. Tyranitar survives any single attack (Light of Ruin max 89.9%, Earthquake max 86.5%), guaranteeing Ice Punch resolves unless double-targeted. Garchomp's Earthquake also damages ally Floette, potentially deterring its use and letting Excadrill survive to attack. Gengar and Gholdengo remain fresh in back as insurance if the double KO fails.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega is Floette-Eternal (Fairy, base 92 Spe, Flower Veil→Mega likely Fairy Aura). Opponent speed tiers: Talonflame 160-195 (Gale Wings priority Brave Bird), Garchomp 134-169 (Jolly LO), Floette 100-158 (Timid), Milotic 101-133 (Bold), Metagross 90-122 (Adamant), Scrafty 78-110 (Careful). My sand Excadrill at 308 outspeeds all non-Tailwind foes; under opponent Tailwind, Garchomp 268-338 and Floette 246-316 both have uncertain speed vs Excadrill 308. Key damage: Tyranitar Ice Punch 4x on Garchomp (72.6-131.1%, possible KO from 90%), Excadrill Iron Head 2x on Floette (79.6-154.4%, possible OHKO from 100%). Floette Light of Ruin on Tyranitar 61.8-89.9% (not OHKO). Garchomp Earthquake on Tyranitar 61.4-86.5% (not OHKO). Combined Light of Ruin + Earthquake on Tyranitar is lethal (123-176%). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is wincon for trapping weakened targets. Plan: keep Sand core as default lead; adjust backs if opponent adapts. Watch for Protect and Tailwind as opponent adaptations in game 2. Gengar and Gholdengo both weak to Ground (Poison/Steel respectively), so Earthquake from Garchomp threatens all team members.

decisions.rationale: Opponent has only Garchomp left at 80% — heavily winning position. Gholdengo is the better send-in over Gengar because Shadow Tag is useless (no switches available), Gholdengo has Recover+Leftovers to outlast Life Orb recoil, and keeping Gengar fresh in back provides insurance. Excadrill at 1% is already a sacrifice piece. Even worst case (Garchomp KOs Excadrill + Gholdengo), Gengar cleans up easily.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Garchomp/Talonflame/Metagross/Floette-Mega. Floette-Mega is Fairy Aura (confirmed). Opponent only has Garchomp (80%, Life Orb) remaining — near-certain win with Gholdengo+Gengar in back. For Game 2: expect opponent to adapt with Protect usage and possibly different lead. Sand core (Tyranitar+Excadrill) remains strong default. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is wincon when opponent has multiple Pokémon remaining. Watch for Tailwind counterplay from opponent. Gholdengo and Gengar both weak to Ground — Earthquake from Garchomp threatens entire team.

selection: Light of Ruin -> foe 1 (Tyranitar) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Mega Light of Ruin plus Dragon Claw concentrates guaranteed combined pressure into Tyranitar before it can remove Garchomp; Mega Floette also gives the best chance to withstand Excadrill's Iron Head if Tyranitar protects.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize removing Tyranitar and Excadrill to end sand and Steel pressure. Mega Floette's Fairy Aura provides major immediate Fairy damage, but preserve it from Steel- and Poison-type attackers whenever possible.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp's Earthquake threatens a possible OHKO on Gholdengo (72.2–104.6%). With only Garchomp remaining at 80%, the series is nearly secured—playing safe is correct. Gholdengo Protects to guarantee it stays at 100% regardless of Garchomp's choice. Excadrill (1 HP) fires High Horsepower into Garchomp for 32.1–56.3% if it moves first, chunking Garchomp to 24–48% for an easy cleanup next turn. Even if Garchomp outspeeds and KOs Excadrill with Earthquake, Gholdengo is preserved at full and Tailwind expires, leaving Gholdengo+Gengar vs a Life Orb–chipped Garchomp with no speed boost—an essentially guaranteed win.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Garchomp/Talonflame/Metagross/Floette-Mega. Floette-Mega confirmed Fairy Aura. Garchomp is Jolly Life Orb with Earthquake/Dragon Claw/Rock Slide/Protect. Opponent only has Garchomp remaining at 80%—near-certain win. For Game 2: expect opponent to adapt leads and Protect usage. Sand core (Tyranitar+Excadrill) remains strong default. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is wincon when opponent has multiple Pokémon remaining. Watch for Tailwind counterplay. Gholdengo and Gengar both weak to Ground—Earthquake from Garchomp threatens entire team; consider Protect reads and positioning.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.
Earthquake is the only play that guaranteed removes 1% Excadrill while also giving Garchomp a meaningful chance to immediately KO Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed Gholdengo with Leftovers and Good as Gold, using Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Protect, and Recover; Excadrill carries consumed Focus Sash and Sand Rush. Their unrevealed fourth is one of Mega Gengar, Grimmsnarl, or Paldean Aqua Tauros.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is the opponent's last Pokémon at 70% HP. Gengar (178) outspeeds Garchomp (134–169) and Mega Evolution pushes Speed to 200 and SpA to 222, still outspeeding. Mega Gengar Shadow Ball (~34–63% est.) plus Gholdengo Make It Rain (35.3–63.9%) totals ~69–127% of Garchomp's max HP, giving ~94% effective KO chance even accounting for Make It Rain's 95% accuracy. Garchomp's Earthquake guarantees KO on Gengar and can OHKO Gholdengo (72–105%), but the probability of both being KO'd AND Garchomp surviving both hits is ~1%. Mega Evolving has no downside here—Shadow Tag is moot with one foe remaining, and the SpA/Speed/Bulk boosts all help. Sludge Bomb is NVE (0.5x) and Taunt doesn't stop Earthquake, so Shadow Ball is the clear best attack. Make It Rain outperforms Gholdengo Shadow Ball despite the 5% miss chance due to higher effective BP.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Garchomp/Talonflame/Metagross/Floette-Mega. Floette-Mega confirmed Fairy Aura. Garchomp is Jolly Life Orb with Earthquake/Dragon Claw/Rock Slide/Protect. Garchomp Earthquake guaranteed OHKO on Gengar and possible OHKO on Gholdengo (72–105% with spread). My Gengar spread confirmed: Timid, 2 HP / 32 SpA / 32 Spe Stat Points (66/66). Mega Gengar stats: HP 137, Atk 76, Def 100, SpA 222, SpD 115, Spe 200. Game 2: Sand core (Tyranitar+Excadrill) remains strong default lead. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is wincon when opponent has multiple Pokémon remaining. Watch for Tailwind counterplay and Earthquake threat to both Gholdengo and Gengar—consider Protect reads and positioning. Gholdengo Make It Rain is stronger than Shadow Ball vs neutral targets despite spread reduction (90 effective BP vs 80).

decisions.rationale: Earthquake is the only play that immediately guarantees the Gengar KO if it does not Protect while also threatening Gholdengo for heavy super-effective damage.
decisions.notebook: Gholdengo: Leftovers, Good as Gold, Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Protect, Recover. Gengar: Gengarite, Cursed Body before Mega Evolution, Sludge Bomb, Shadow Ball, Taunt, Protect. Excadrill: Focus Sash, Sand Rush, Iron Head, High Horsepower, Rock Slide, Protect. Tyranitar: Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect.

reflections.summary: Won through favorable trades and opponent self-damage. Garchomp's Earthquake friendly-fired Metagross (super effective), accelerating its KO. Sandstorm chip finished sashed Talonflame after Rock Slide broke the sash. The trade sequence left Garchomp alone; Gholdengo survived the final Earthquake at 10% and finished it with Make It Rain. Gengar-Mega contributed only chip damage before dying to Earthquake—Shadow Tag was never utilized since opponent had one Pokémon left when it entered.
reflections.adjustment: Gengar-Mega is extremely vulnerable to Garchomp Earthquake and should not be brought in while Garchomp is on the field unless Protect is guaranteed. Prioritize removing or weakening Garchomp before Gengar enters, or lead Gengar-Mega early to trap and remove a target before Earthquake pressure mounts. Consider Protect reads on Garchomp to create safe Gengar turns.
reflections.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brought Garchomp/Talonflame/Metagross/Floette-Mega; left Milotic and Scrafty in back. Floette-Mega confirmed Fairy Aura, Timid, Floettite, Light of Ruin OHKOs Tyranitar. Garchomp is Jolly Life Orb with Earthquake/Dragon Claw/Rock Slide/Protect; Earthquake friendly-fires teammates (hit Metagross SE). Talonflame is Jolly Focus Sash Gale Wings with Tailwind/Brave Bird/Flare Blitz/Taunt; Sandstorm chip finishes sashed Talonflame. Metagross is Adamant Lum Berry Clear Body with Meteor Mash/Zen Headbutt/Bullet Punch/Protect. Gholdengo barely survived Garchomp Earthquake spread at 10%—Earthquake is a critical threat to both Gengar and Gholdengo. Game 2: Sand core (Tyranitar+Excadrill) remains strong default lead. Opponent may adjust by bringing Milotic (Competitive, Scald/Icy Wind/Recover/Protect) or Scrafty (Intimidate, Fake Out/Snarl/Drain Punch/Protect) for game 2. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is wincon when opponent has multiple Pokémon remaining—do not waste it as a last-mon revenge killer. Gholdengo Make It Rain stronger than Shadow Ball vs neutral targets despite spread reduction (90 effective BP vs 80). Watch for Tailwind counterplay and Protect reads on Garchomp.

reflections.summary: Lost to the Tyranitar–Excadrill sand mode's favorable trades: Rock Slide plus sand removed Focus Sash Talonflame immediately, High Horsepower removed Metagross, and Excadrill's Iron Head removed Mega Floette. Garchomp then nearly reversed the endgame but was finished by Gholdengo's Make It Rain. The four brought were only partly suited: Garchomp and Floette pressured Tyranitar, but Talonflame's Sash was unreliable in sand and Metagross was exposed to Excadrill. Mega Floette was a reasonable Mega choice for Tyranitar pressure, but it needed protection from Iron Head.
reflections.adjustment: Against the sand lead, preserve Floette with Protect while using Garchomp to pressure or remove Excadrill first; do not commit both attacks into Tyranitar while Excadrill can freely Iron Head Floette. Favor a Garchomp-centered lead over Talonflame–Metagross when expecting Tyranitar–Excadrill.
reflections.notebook: Opponent used a Tyranitar–Excadrill sand lead; Smooth Rock Tyranitar supports Sand Rush Excadrill. Their game-1 four were Tyranitar, Excadrill, Leftovers Gholdengo, and Mega Gengar. Gholdengo can Protect/Recover to extend endgames and carries Make It Rain and Shadow Ball; Mega Gengar has Taunt, Protect, Shadow Ball, and Sludge Bomb. Future plan: prioritize Excadrill before exposing Mega Floette, and do not rely on Talonflame's Focus Sash while sand is active.
